It is the only vegetable oil that can be consumed exactly as it is obtained. It comes directly from olives through a mechanical extraction process — rather more involved than simply squeezing an orange. When the olives arrive at the mill, they are first cleaned to remove leaves, small twigs and other material collected during harvesting. Once clean, they are ready for extraction, a process that consists essentially of four stages. Constituyen el sistema utilizado en nues: A Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) recognises products whose distinctive qualities are linked to the geographical area where the raw materials are produced and the product is made, together with the expertise of the people involved. Producers covered by a PDO must follow defined specifications designed to maintain consistently high standards. Compliance is supervised by an authorised regulatory body, and Spanish PDOs are protected under European Union rules.
Al consumidor, fundamentalmente para gar: For customers, a PDO provides assurance of specific characteristics and a consistently high standard of quality. For producers, it protects the recognised name against similar products made elsewhere and can help them reach new markets under the PDO quality guarantee.
Nuestros cerdos de raza 100% ibérica nac: Our 100% Iberian pigs are born outdoors and are suckled by their mothers until they are old enough to fend for themselves and begin feeding on the resources of the dehesa. Piglets born in autumn may taste their first acorns during weaning, although most of the crop is reserved for the older pigs entering the montanera finishing season. During this period they typically grow from around 90–100 kg to 170–180 kg, feeding on acorns, grass and other natural resources from the dehesa, such as mushrooms, roots and tubers.
¿De qué se alimentan los cerdos antes de: What do the pigs eat before the finishing period?
Se alimentan de los recursos de la dehes: They feed on the natural resources of the dehesa. In summer, when these are scarcer, their diet is supplemented mainly with cereals and pulses. The farmers sow crops such as chickpeas, broad beans, vetch and oats so that, when summer arrives, the pigs can feed on them

Temperatura, humedad y tiempo de madurac: Temperature, humidity and ageing time for hams and shoulders.
El proceso de elaboración de nuestros ja: Our hams and shoulders go through several stages. The first is salting, carried out at very low temperature and high humidity. Depending on the weight of the piece, this lasts around two weeks. After a resting period in temperature- and humidity-controlled chambers, the pieces move to natural curing cellars, where temperatures range from around 18–20°C in summer to 10–12°C in winter. This slow curing process allows for long, optimal maturation — more than 30 months for the hams — and develops aromas that cannot be achieved through accelerated curing.
